title: About System Logs - AI Infra Scanning

blocks.text: The System Logs page with AI Infra Scanning tab in AI Security gives administrators a unified, filterable view of every AI infrastructure scan event generated across their AWS, Azure, and GCP environments. The page displays scan outcomes, including successes, failures, and detailed error messages so administrators can quickly triage scan health, identify misconfigurations, and audit the inventory pipeline over time.
The System Logs Page in AI Security provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: View error events in chronological order across AWS, Azure, and GCP from a single page.
See inline scan error messages and correlate them to parent resources without leaving the console or engaging support.
Filter scan activity by cloud environment, region, resource type, severity, resource status, and time range to quickly isolate issues.
Export filtered scan event logs to CSV files to support compliance requirements, covering up to 30 days of scan history.
Detect and resolve misconfigurations blocking scans such as missing customer-managed KMS keys independently, without engineering involvement.

blocks.heading: About System Logs - AI Infrastructure Scanning Page

blocks.text: On the System Logs - AI Infrastructure Scanning page (Administration > System Logs - AI Infrastructure Scanning), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Search by resource name, resource ID, or message.
Filter
Time Range: Filters the results by a predefined time period. Select Last 1 Hour, Last 1 Day, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days, or All Time.
Environment: Filters scan events by cloud provider environment. Select AWS, Azure, GCP, Copilot Studio, GitHub, or GitLab to narrow results to a specific cloud environment.
Regions: Filters scan events by the cloud region where the scanned resource is deployed, e.g., us-east-1.
Source: Filters scan events by the type of cloud resource that was scanned, e.g., AWS::EC2::Volume.
Severity: Filters scan events by the severity level of the scan error. Select Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Unknown.
Source Status: Filters scan events based on the current status of the scanned resource. Select one or all of the following:
Active: To view events for existing resources.
Deleted: To view events for resources that have been removed.
the report.
Export the event results as a CSV file to your default downloads folder. You can also view the downloaded results in the Report Management page.
Select and hide columns in the table.
Show or hide filters.
View a list of scan events and for each event you can view:
Timestamp: The date and time the last full scan was initiated for the resource, formatted as local date and time in the user's time zone.
Event ID: The unique identifier assigned to the scan event record.
Source ID & Name: The unique identifier and name of the scanned resource, e.g., an ARN or URN for AWS resources.
Source Type: The type of cloud resource that was scanned, e.g., AWS::EC2::Volume).
Severity: The severity level of the scan event, derived from the scan error or resource tag.
Event Details: A comma-separated list of scan error messages and descriptions associated with the resource's latest scan attempt.
Region: The cloud region where the resource is deployed.
Environment: The cloud provider environment in which the resource exists.
Provider Timestamp: The timestamp of the event as recorded by the cloud service provider.
Source Status: The current status of the resource.
Parent Source ID: The unique identifier of the parent resource associated with this event.
The following columns are hidden. You can enable the hidden columns by clicking the gear icon and selecting the column names.
